Subject: Request: Evidence pack for data export controls and technical safeguards

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the discussion yesterday. As part of our vendor review for handling patient-identifiable data, our procurement and privacy teams need a compact evidence pack that covers cross-border data export safeguards and the operational controls you use to meet DPF/DPA expectations. Specifically, could you provide the following: 

- A one-page technical assertion describing how Redwood protects exported personal data (encryption, pseudonymization, KMS, access controls).
- A sample access log (redacted) covering token and API access to show audit fields and retention windows.
- The list of sub-processors and regions where Sunridge data might be processed or cached.
- Confirmation of the contractual mechanism you propose for EU->US transfers (SCCs / adequacy / DPF status) and any draft DPA annex items we should expect.

We appreciate a 48-72 hour turnaround if possible. We will treat the materials as confidential.

Regards,
Ellie Graham
Senior Procurement Manager
Sunridge Health
procurement@sunridgehealth.com

Subject: Re: Request: Evidence pack for data export controls and technical safeguards

Hi Ellie —

Thanks for the clear list. I've attached a compact technical assertion and a draft SCC execution template that outline our contractual approach. Highlights below: 

- Transfers & legal mechanism: We recommend executing the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) as processor-to-controller addenda for Sunridge, with an optional DPF-ready supplement we maintain internally.
- Technical safeguards: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, application-level pseudonymization options (customer-configurable), and per-tenant customer-managed KMS support (bring-your-own-key via supported KMS providers).
- Operational controls: Role-based access control with approval flows, just-in-time privileges for sensitive datasets, continuous audit logs stored for 18 months (configurable for enterprise plans).
- Sub-processors & regions: We included an excerpt of our current sub-processor list and region map in the assertion. Primary processing occurs in EU (Frankfurt, Dublin) and US (us-west2) regions; caching may occur in additional regions for latency-sensitive requests — always under contractual and technical safeguards.

Please find attached: redwood-dpf-technical-assertion-20280214.pdf; scc-execution-draft.docx.

I'll loop Monica (Security & Trust) and Neha (Privacy) for any technical follow-ups; they can provide the redacted logs and KMS matrix you asked for.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
